subject: Daz
fact: Daz is maintaining a fabricated identity as a Lolth-follower to Asha Vandree, a belief he has cultivated long enough to treat as consistent characterization rather than deception. He refuses to hide during combat, prioritizing participation over Nym Duskryn’s contractual interests. He is aware of what he has lost, what Menzoberranzan made him, and what he now believes about slavery and freedom, but he allows Asha’s belief to stand because it is load-bearing in this moment.
source_quote: I have been maintaining a Lolth-follower identity with Asha Vandree for long enough that the fiction has its own momentum — you learn to stop thinking of it as lying and start thinking of it as consistent characterization.

subject: Nym Duskryn
fact: Nym Duskryn was contracted to extract Daz alive for payment. She views his actions as complicating her mission and expresses frustration through professional detachment. Her question — 'Can I kill your brother?' — reveals a shift from exasperated professionalism to targeted pragmatism, redirecting her irritation toward an available tactical target.
source_quote: Can you please keep your head down and out of combat? We only get paid if you live.

subject: Kaelira Duskryn
fact: Kaelira Duskryn is Nym’s partner in the extraction contract. She physically hauls Daz to safety through toxic gas, demonstrating urgency and enforcement of survival, but her actions are bound by the same transactional framework as Nym’s. She does not question Daz’s defiance — she acts on the imperative to deliver him alive.
source_quote: Come with me if you want to live, you idiot.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a devoted follower of Lolth who immediately identifies Daz and his companions as potential traitors. Her rigid worldview contains a pre-established slot for 'Lolth-aligned drow who are here to help,' which Daz exploits. Her belief in this identity is not questioned — it is weaponized as a tactical necessity.
source_quote: Who are you? You must be traitors! Traitors to Lolth!

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes the unfolding situation with the steady, clear-eyed precision of a record-keeper. He notes that Asha’s characterization of Daz as an 'insane mage who converted to Lolthism' accurately describes the fiction being maintained. His commentary is not emotional, but factual — he is documenting the lie as if it were data.
source_quote: The situation was 'accurately described' by Asha's characterization of me as an insane mage who had converted to Lolthism.

subject: Duskryn Sisters
fact: The Duskryn sisters (Nym and Kaelira) operate as a contracted extraction unit under a mercenary arrangement to deliver Daz alive. Their loyalty is to the contract, not to Daz’s cause. Their professionalism is undermined by his refusal to comply with their survival protocol, creating tension between contractual duty and tactical reality.
source_quote: We only get paid if you live.

subject: T'sarran Soldiers
fact: The T'sarran soldiers are elite drow reinforcements who accepted a contract to resolve a crisis but are now paralyzed by logistical failure — specifically, the absence of Dispel Magic. They are trained, armored, and numerically superior, yet they stall at the tunnel mouth debating tactics while environmental hazards and enemy magic escalate. Their failure is not heroic, but petty and bureaucratic.
source_quote: I thought you said this was going to be an easy kill. And you don't have a Dispel Magic. So I have to go through this. I don't know what else to tell you.

subject: Corrupted High Priestess
fact: The corrupted high priestess is engaged in active combat with Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir. She is a major threat, likely responsible for the field of biting insects and the influx of Drow reinforcements. Her presence defines the battlefield’s lethality and the urgency of Daz’s refusal to stand aside.
source_quote: Thorin and Grygum and Zalthir are in active combat with a corrupted high priestess and a field of biting insects and what appears to be an inexhaustible supply of Drow reinforcements.

subject: Biting Insects
fact: A field of biting insects surrounds the battlefield, contributing to the lethal environment and impeding movement. They are part of the corrupted high priestess’s domain, acting as a non-magical but persistent hazard that compounds the tactical challenges faced by all combatants.
source_quote: Thorin and Grygum and Zalthir are in active combat with a corrupted high priestess and a field of biting insects...

subject: Drow Reinforcements
fact: An inexhaustible supply of Drow reinforcements continues to emerge, overwhelming the battlefield’s defenses. They are not merely additional combatants but a symbol of the enemy’s resilience and the escalating stakes. Their presence justifies Daz’s decision to remain in the fight — standing idle would be unacceptable.
source_quote: ...what appears to be an inexhaustible supply of Drow reinforcements.

subject: lightning bolt misfire
fact: A mage launched a lightning bolt into the cavern with real commitment, but it struck only open air. The misfire represents wasted power and the chaotic unpredictability of combat under pressure, reinforcing the sense that even powerful magic is ineffective without precise targeting or situational awareness.
source_quote: The mage launched a lightning bolt into the cavern with real commitment. It hit nothing. Just open air and ambition.

subject: contract viability
fact: Nym Duskryn is calculating whether her contract is still viable, given Daz’s refusal to comply with extraction protocol. Her question — 'Can I kill your brother?' — signals a potential shift from extraction to termination, raising the question of whether Daz’s survival is now incompatible with mission success.

subject: identity as armor
fact: Daz’s fabricated identity as a Lolth-follower is not just deception — it is psychological armor, a strategic framework that allows him to navigate Asha’s worldview. The thread remains unresolved: how long can this fiction hold before it fractures under pressure, and what happens when Asha discovers the truth?
source_quote: I know what's real... But right now, in this cavern, Asha thinks I serve Lolth, and that belief is load-bearing.

subject: the cavern
fact: The cavern is the central battleground where Daz, his allies, the Duskryn sisters, the T'sarran soldiers, and the corrupted high priestess converge. It is filled with toxic gas, biting insects, arcane flares, and the echoes of failed spells. Its environment is hostile, claustrophobic, and charged with tactical chaos.
source_quote: She was hauling me northeast through the chittering wall of it while the poisonous gas did its work on both of us.

subject: the tunnel mouth
fact: The tunnel mouth is the choke point where the T'sarran soldiers are stalled, debating tactics while the battle rages behind them. It symbolizes the failure of elite forces to adapt — they possess the tools but lack the flexibility to overcome a simple spell deficiency.
source_quote: They were busy at the tunnel mouth having an argument that I can only describe as profoundly unhelpful given the circumstances.

subject: shield ward
fact: Daz’s shield ward activated reflexively before his conscious mind decided to cast it. This object represents the body’s ingrained combat training — a mechanical reaction that saved his life. It is not magic he chose, but magic that chose him.
source_quote: The first bolt hit my shield ward before I'd consciously decided to cast it.

subject: spell slot
fact: The spell slot expended to activate the shield ward is a measurable cost — one resource traded for survival. It is a quiet but critical detail in the ledger of Daz’s combat decisions, illustrating how every action in battle consumes finite capacity.
source_quote: The cost was one spell slot. The benefit was that I was still standing.

subject: session time
fact: The events occur during an active combat session, marked by the passage of seconds — two seconds before Asha’s accusation became catastrophic, moments of hesitation before Daz speaks his defiance. Time is measured not in hours or days, but in the urgency of reactions and the weight of unspoken choices.
source_quote: There was a window of perhaps two seconds before this became catastrophic.
